blocks.text:
(PT) Private Transfers + Domestic Flight (Not Included) + Mérida City TourDuration: Flight approximately 2 hours + City Tour 2.5–3 hoursLanguages: English and Spanish

Today you leave behind the vibrant energy of Mexico City and travel to Mérida, the elegant and sun-drenched capital of the Yucatán Peninsula, often called La Ciudad Blanca (The White City).

Your day begins with a private transfer to Mexico City International Airport. After your domestic flight (not included), a driver will be waiting to greet you upon arrival in Mérida and take you comfortably to your hotel located in the historic center.

Once settled, discover the city’s unique blend of colonial architecture and Mayan heritage on a guided walking tour through the Centro Histórico. Highlights include the Cathedral of San Ildefonso, the colorful Zócalo, and the elegant façades that line the historic streets. The tour also includes a visit to Paseo de Montejo, Mérida’s grand boulevard inspired by European architecture.

Tour start times are available at 13:00, 16:00, or 18:00 hours.

Included:• Private transfers in Mexico City and Mérida• Certified bilingual guide for the city tour• Overnight stay in Mérida

Not Included:• Domestic flight (available upon request)• Meals• Tips• Personal expenses

The journey then continues to Teotihuacan, the legendary “City of the Gods.” Walk along the famous Avenue of the Dead and marvel at the enormous Pyramids of the Sun and the Moon, two of the most iconic structures of ancient Mesoamerica. With your expert guide’s explanations, the ancient city comes alive as you learn about its sophisticated engineering, cosmic alignments, mythology, and the powerful civilization that once thrived here long before the Aztecs.
Included:• Shared transportation• Certified bilingual guide• Entrance to Teotihuacan• Visit to the Basilica of Guadalupe• Overnight stay in Mexico City

paragraphs.text: Your exploration begins at Uxmal, a UNESCO World Heritage Site celebrated for its elegant architecture and remarkable decorative details. Walk through this magnificent ancient city and admire iconic structures such as the Pyramid of the Magician, the grand Governor’s Palace, and the beautifully carved Nunnery Quadrangle, each reflecting the sophistication of Maya artistry, astronomy, and ceremonial life.
Continue to the nearby archaeological site of Kabah, known for its striking stone façades covered with intricate sculptures and masks dedicated to the rain god Chaac.
